title: Seventh Word Interpreting The Comparison Death Belief Patience And Reliance

questions.question: In the comparison, who does the soldier stand for?
questions.answer: He stands for each human being.

questions.question: What does the lion represent?
questions.answer: It represents a person’s appointed time to die.

questions.question: What does the gallows represent in this passage?
questions.answer: It represents death, fading away, and being separated from loved ones.

questions.question: What do the two wounds stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for human weakness and human neediness.

questions.question: What does the long journey symbolize?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the human life journey and what comes after it, from the earliest stage of life all the way to resurrection and crossing the Sirat.

questions.question: What are the two talismans explained in the passage?
questions.answer: They are belief in Allah and belief in the hereafter.

questions.question: How does belief in the hereafter change the meaning of death for a believer?
questions.answer: It turns death into a means of reaching mercy, Paradise, and nearness to Allah instead of something only frightening.

questions.question: According to the passage, why did some wise people come to love death?
questions.answer: They understood its true meaning for believers and saw it as a passage to something better.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah change the way a person looks at passing time and separation?
questions.answer: It helps a person see these changes as chances to notice Allah’s beautiful works, power, and mercy.

questions.question: What example is used to show that change can lead to more beauty?
questions.answer: The passage uses the example of changing reflections and changing scenes that produce better and more beautiful images.

questions.question: What main lesson is being taught through all these symbols?
questions.answer: Faith changes painful and scary realities into meaningful and hopeful ones.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to at the beginning of the target passage?
questions.answer: The speaker is addressing the self, or nafs.

questions.question: What does the passage say about that self’s earlier attitude and later feeling?
questions.answer: It says the self once laughed carelessly but later cried over that laughter.

questions.question: In this explanation, what does the soldier teach us about ourselves?
questions.answer: He teaches that the story is really about the condition of every human being.

questions.question: Why is the lion a fitting symbol in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows death as something always near and impossible to escape.

questions.question: Why is the gallows connected with both death and separation?
questions.answer: Because people not only die, but also lose loved ones as time passes.

questions.question: What human realities are described by the two wounds?
questions.answer: They are our deep weakness and our great need.

questions.question: How wide is the journey described in the passage?
questions.answer: It stretches from before birth through life, the grave, the intermediate stage, resurrection, and the Sirat.

questions.question: Which two beliefs are presented as the answer to this difficult human condition?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the hereafter.

questions.question: What happens to the image of death when the hereafter is believed in?
questions.answer: It becomes like a ride carrying the believer out of this world’s prison to the gardens of Paradise.

questions.question: What new meaning does faith in Allah give to the changes of day and night and the passing of life?
questions.answer: It makes them signs of Allah’s ongoing creation, mercy, and artistry.

questions.question: What idea is expressed by the final Arabic sentence in the target passage?
questions.answer: It expresses that we belong to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of explaining the symbols in the story?
questions.answer: It is to show what the parts of the story mean for real human life.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the true meaning of the soldier?
questions.answer: The soldier means the human being.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the lion in the symbolic explanation?
questions.answer: It means the time of death that has been set for each person.

questions.question: What three ideas are gathered into the symbol of the gallows?
questions.answer: Death, decline, and separation.

questions.question: What are the two painful conditions represented by the wounds?
questions.answer: They are unlimited weakness and deep poverty or need.

questions.question: What stages are included in the exile-like journey?
questions.answer: It includes the spirit world, the womb, childhood, old age, worldly life, the grave, the intermediate realm, resurrection, and the Sirat.

questions.question: What are the two sacred means that answer these hardships?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah and faith in the hereafter.

questions.question: How is death described after the second talisman takes effect?
questions.answer: It is described as something controlled and beneficial, carrying the believer to a better home.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about wise people who understood death correctly?
questions.answer: It suggests they no longer saw it only as a terror and even longed for it before it came.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can a believer notice in the changing world through belief in Allah?
questions.answer: A believer can notice Allah’s artistry, power, and mercy in the constant changes of creation.

questions.question: What overall contrast does the passage make between life without faith and life with faith?
questions.answer: Without faith, human life looks helpless and frightening; with faith, it becomes meaningful, hopeful, and full of signs of Allah.

questions.question: In the target passage, what does the speaker want the nafs to understand first?
questions.answer: The speaker wants it to understand that the story is really about itself and all people.

questions.question: What future event is represented by the lion?
questions.answer: It represents the arrival of death at its appointed time.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the gallows to everyday human experience?
questions.answer: It connects it to the way people keep losing others as time passes from day to night.

questions.question: What do the two wounds reveal about human nature?
questions.answer: They reveal that people are naturally weak and deeply in need.

questions.question: Why is the journey called long in this symbolic explanation?
questions.answer: Because it includes many stages before birth, during life, and after death.

questions.question: Which two beliefs are called talismans?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the hereafter.

questions.question: What change does belief in the hereafter bring to the meaning of death?
questions.answer: It changes death from something like destruction into a way to reach Allah’s mercy and Paradise.

questions.question: Why would wise people desire death after understanding it properly?
questions.answer: Because they see it as a doorway to eternal mercy rather than a final loss.

questions.question: What does belief in Allah allow a person to do when looking at the world’s constant changes?
questions.answer: It allows the person to enjoy thinking about Allah’s beautiful and ever-renewed works.

questions.question: What do the examples of changing reflections and changing scenes help explain?
questions.answer: They help explain that renewal and change can bring fresh beauty instead of only loss.

questions.question: What feeling does the passage try to build in the believer: hopelessness or hope?
questions.answer: It builds hope.

questions.question: Whom is the symbolic soldier said to represent?
questions.answer: He represents every person.

questions.question: What does the lion symbolize in one short phrase?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the appointed hour of death.

questions.question: What does the gallows symbolize besides death itself?
questions.answer: It also symbolizes decline and parting from others.

questions.question: What is the first wound a symbol of?
questions.answer: It is a symbol of human helplessness.

questions.question: What is the second wound a symbol of?
questions.answer: It is a symbol of human poverty and need.

questions.question: What does the exile-like trip represent?
questions.answer: It represents the full journey of human existence through many stages until the next life.

questions.question: What are the two beliefs that solve the problem in the story?
questions.answer: They are faith in Allah and faith in the hereafter.

questions.question: How is death reimagined for the believer through faith in the hereafter?
questions.answer: It is reimagined as a safe and useful ride toward Paradise and the mercy of Allah.

questions.question: What attitude toward death is mentioned for those who truly understand it?
questions.answer: They may welcome it instead of only fearing it.

questions.question: How does faith in Allah change the meaning of passing time?
questions.answer: It turns it into an opportunity to witness Allah’s signs and creative beauty.

questions.question: What key message about dunya and akhirah can be inferred from this passage?
questions.answer: This world is temporary, but faith helps a person see the path to the next world with peace and purpose.

questions.question: What personal lesson is given by saying that the soldier is you and mankind?
questions.answer: The lesson is that the story describes our own real condition, not just someone else’s.

questions.question: What danger does the lion point to in human life?
questions.answer: It points to the certainty that death will come at its fixed time.

questions.question: Why is the gallows an especially strong symbol in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows not only dying but also the pain of watching things fade and loved ones leave.

questions.question: What do the two wounds teach about what people cannot escape on their own?
questions.answer: They teach that people cannot escape their weakness and need.

questions.question: How far does the journey extend according to the passage?
questions.answer: It extends from the earliest beginning of human life to resurrection and crossing the Sirat.

questions.question: Which two beliefs are presented as sacred helps for this journey?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the hereafter.

questions.question: What transformation happens to death through belief in the hereafter?
questions.answer: It becomes a means of transport from this world to the mercy of Allah and the gardens of Paradise.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about people who only see death as the end?
questions.answer: It implies they have not understood its true reality for believers.

questions.question: Through belief in Allah, what can a person enjoy in the changing world?
questions.answer: A person can enjoy reflecting on Allah’s power, mercy, and beautiful creation.

questions.question: How do the examples at the end support the idea of constant renewal?
questions.answer: They show that when one image passes and another comes, a more beautiful display can appear.

questions.question: What is one central message of the whole target passage?
questions.answer: True faith gives meaning to suffering, change, death, and the journey ahead.
